glossary.title: Important terms
glossary.intro: A short explanation of the people and roles that appear in the application.
glossary.disclaimer: These explanations are intended for orientation in the application and do not replace legal advice or a formal determination of authority.

employer.title: Employer
employer.summary: The person who employs the caregiver and is responsible for managing the employment.
employer.details: The employer is responsible for matters including the employment agreement, salary and rights, document retention, and required reports and payments. The employer may be the care recipient or another person managing the employment on their behalf.

caregiver.title: Caregiver
caregiver.summary: The employee who provides assistance and care to the care recipient as part of an employment relationship.
caregiver.details: The caregiver has rights and obligations under the employment terms and applicable law. The application stores their employment details, documents, tasks, and payroll calculations.

representative.title: Authorized representative
representative.summary: The main contact the employer chose to save for assistance and coordination.
representative.details: The representative may be a family member or another helper who receives updates or assists with ongoing management, as decided by the employer.
representative.note: In the current version this is a saved contact only. Saving the contact does not grant account access, signing authority, or legal authority.

additionalRepresentative.title: Additional representative
additionalRepresentative.summary: An additional contact who can assist, act as backup, or handle a particular matter.
additionalRepresentative.details: An additional representative can be saved when more than one person assists the employer. Their responsibilities should be clearly divided to prevent duplicated or missed tasks.
additionalRepresentative.note: The additional representative is also a contact only unless separate, explicit authorization has been granted outside the application.

guidePage.kicker: A practical guide for employing families
guidePage.title: Direct caregiver employment — what should you manage?
guidePage.intro: Direct employment involves several parallel processes. An organized list, clear dates and consistent records make it easier to see what is complete and what still needs attention.
guidePage.section1Title: 1. Employment details and the people involved
guidePage.section1Body: Start with employer, care recipient and caregiver details, the employment start date and an authorized contact. The rest of the system relies on this information.
guidePage.section2Body: Record each document's name, type, expiry date and current status. An early reminder helps start renewal work before expiry but does not replace checking with the relevant authority.
guidePage.section3Body: Record policy periods and align tracking with the employment start date. Before changes or renewals, verify coverage requirements with the insurer or another qualified source.
guidePage.section4Body: A clear calculation separates base pay, Saturdays or rest days, additions and deductions. Saved monthly summaries create an annual record and a clear copy for employer and caregiver.
guidePage.section5Body: Organize monthly, quarterly and annual tasks by opening and deadline dates. This distinguishes tasks that are not open yet, open tasks and items that need attention.
guidePage.noticeBody: Rules, rates and deadlines can change. CareDesk helps organize and document; verify information with an official source or qualified professional before financial or legal action.
guidePage.ctaTitle: Want to turn the list into a workflow?
guidePage.ctaBody: CareDesk presents information in short screens with tasks, reminders and summaries.
